CausalChain: Radiotherapy -> Tumor cell death and release of immunogenic factors (including a transient TGF‐β1 surge) -> Acute systemic TGF‐β1 peak primes CD8+ T cells into a reversible pre‐exhausted state (detected via single-cell transcriptomics and real-time cytokine monitoring) -> Timed PD-1 blockade administered when pre‐exhausted T cells are present -> Reinvigoration of CD8+ T cells and enhanced anti-tumor immune response
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that radiotherapy in solid tumors induces a transient, yet distinct, systemic increase in TGF‐β1 that primes a subset of CD8+ T cells into a reversible pre‐exhausted state, identifiable through advanced single-cell transcriptomic profiling and real-time cytokine monitoring. By leveraging contemporary technologies such as high-sensitivity TGF‐β1 assays and machine learning algorithms to accurately define this temporal window, administering PD‐1 inhibitors at this strategic juncture will optimally re‐activate the primed T cells, thereby enhancing anti-tumor immunity and improving clinical outcomes. This approach incorporates dynamic biomarker monitoring and precision timing to overcome the traditional immunosuppressive challenges of TGF‐β1 and conventional combination therapy paradigms.
Abstract: This study proposes an innovative, time‐optimized immunotherapeutic strategy for solid tumors by integrating radiotherapy with real‐time immune biomarker monitoring. Specifically, radiotherapy is posited to induce tumor cell death and the release of immunogenic factors, including a transient, moderate surge of circulating TGF‐β1. Advanced single‐cell transcriptomics, combined with real‐time cytokine assays and machine learning algorithms, will be employed to delineate a precise post‐radiotherapy window during which CD8+ T cells enter a reversible ‘pre‐exhausted’ state. Administering PD‐1 inhibitors during this defined temporal window is hypothesized to effectively reinvigorate these primed T cells, thereby amplifying anti‐tumor immunity and leading to improved clinical outcomes.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis maintains the original causal steps: radiotherapy-induced tumor cell death, TGF‐β1-mediated priming of a state of reversible T cell exhaustion, detection of this state via single-cell transcriptomics, and the timing of PD-1 blockade to reinvigorate these cells. However, it refines and expands upon the original by incorporating real-time high-sensitivity assays for TGF‐β1, the use of machine learning to accurately determine the optimal therapeutic window, and a more precise definition of the ‘pre‐exhausted’ T cell state through multi-omic profiling. These enhancements address previous gaps regarding temporal dynamics and biomarker specificity, thereby improving the practical implementability and translational impact of the therapeutic strategy.
